title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
abstract: arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. translated_title: 世界不会等待：在实时时钟下评估与训练智能体
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体能够解决复杂的交互式任务，但推理和工具调用需要时间。在持续变化的环境中，原本正确的动作可能来得太迟。我们提出了RealtimeBench，包含六种游戏类型的180个任务，用于在推理过程中游戏持续运行的情况下评估智能体。配对评估显示，GPT-6.1-sol在游戏暂停时优于速度更快的Jev，但在游戏持续运行时却落后于Jev。我们提出了双时间尺度离线递归自我改进（TORSI）：一个较慢的教师智能体在两次尝试之间研究失败案例并在暂停的游戏中测试修正方案，然后为较快的学生智能体编写可复用的指令。学生在游戏过程中无需调用教师即可自主行动，验证分数决定哪些更新被采纳。两轮改进使Jev在0-100进度量表上的平均测试分数从13.51提升至24.19，在所有六种游戏类型上均有提升。这些指令还能提高平均得分。
tldr: 该论文提出了RealtimeBench实时基准和TORSI双时间尺度自我改进方法，通过慢教师编写可复用指令、快学生无需教师调用即可自主行动的框架，使更快的智能体在实时变化的环境中胜过更强但更慢的模型。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces RealtimeBench and TORSI, a two-timescale offline recursive self-improvement framework where a slow teacher distills reusable instructions for a fast student agent, enabling the faster agent to outperform stronger-but-slower models in live, continuously changing environments.
